official_tasks.task: Build an agentic loop that keeps iterating while the stop reason signals a tool request and ends when the model signals it is done, feeding tool results back each turn.
Structure a hub-and-spoke multi-agent system in which a coordinator decomposes the query, picks subagents dynamically, aggregates results, and refines until coverage is adequate.
Configure subagent spawning and context passing, remembering that subagents start with isolated context and need findings passed explicitly, with parallel spawns in a single response.
Enforce multi-step workflow ordering and escalation handoffs with programmatic prerequisites rather than prompt wording, and compile structured handoff summaries for human agents.
Use SDK hooks to normalize tool results before the model sees them and to intercept outgoing tool calls that violate business rules, redirecting to an alternative workflow.
Choose between fixed prompt chains and adaptive decomposition for a workflow, including per-file review passes plus a cross-file integration pass.
Manage session state by resuming named sessions, forking from a shared baseline, and deciding between resume and a fresh session seeded with a summary when tool results are stale.
Give each agent a scoped tool set, avoid tool overload, and use tool_choice (auto, any, forced) to control whether and which tool is called.
Decide between plan mode and direct execution by task complexity and use the Explore subagent to keep verbose discovery out of the main context.

Define escalation and ambiguity rules: escalate on explicit human request, policy gaps or stalled progress, ask for more identifiers on multiple matches, and distrust sentiment or self-confidence proxies.
Propagate errors across agents with structured context (failure type, attempt, partial results, alternatives), avoiding both silent suppression and whole-workflow aborts.
Manage context in large-codebase exploration with scratchpad files, subagent delegation, phase summaries, manifest-based crash recovery, and compaction.
Choose among workflow, agentic and augmented-LLM architectural patterns for a given use case.
Design multi-agent systems and the orchestration strategy that coordinates them.
Assess an agent or tool configuration for capability bloat and excess permissions.
Choose the integration mechanism (MCP, API/CLI, agent-to-agent) for a situation.
Apply human-in-the-loop validation strategies.
Document architectures and give implementation guidance.
Support lifecycle phases from discovery and design through handoff, monitoring and iteration.
Decide when human review or extra verification is required.
Decide when to use a workflow versus an agent and structure manager/supervisor hierarchies with subagents.
Construct agents with the Claude Agent SDK or custom loops and harnesses, choose self-hosted or Anthropic-hosted deployment, and use hooks for deterministic actions.
Apply common agent patterns (tool-use loops, subagents, memory, context management) and agentic frameworks such as Strands, LangGraph and PydanticAI.

Operate Claude Code core pieces (rules, skills, commands, agents, agent memory) and features such as sessions, slash commands, headless and streaming modes and auto mode, plus repo initialization and settings.json.
Control context with window management, drift and bloat prevention (tool-output pruning, compaction) and isolation via subagents or multi-step workflows.
Implement tools well: function calling, tool descriptions, error handling, dispatch in an agentic harness, client-side vs server-side tools, approval patterns and tool set construction.

docs_facts.fact: The tool that spawns subagents is named Agent; it was renamed from Task in v2.1.63 and old Task(...) references still work as aliases. In SDK streams tool_use blocks say Agent while the system:init tools list may still say Task, so match both. Restrict spawnable types with Agent(agent_type) in tools (only for an agent running as main thread via claude --agent). A subagent can spawn further subagents up to depth 3 by default (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH); 20 concurrent by default (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS).
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Task to Agent rename (v2.1.63) and nested-subagent support; older material says subagents cannot spawn subagents.

docs_facts.fact: Markdown with YAML frontmatter; body is the system prompt. Only name and description required. Fields: tools, disallowedTools, model (sonnet, opus, haiku, fable, full ID, inherit), permissionMode, maxTurns, skills, mcpServers, hooks, memory (user/project/local), background, omitClaudeMd, effort, isolation (worktree), color, initialPrompt. Priority on name clash: managed, --agents flag, .claude/agents/, ~/.claude/agents/, plugin agents/. Each subagent starts with fresh context; only its final message returns to the parent. Built-ins: Explore, Plan, general-purpose.

Define subagents with the agents option on query() (AgentDefinition: description and prompt required; tools, disallowedTools, model, skills, memory, mcpServers, maxTurns, background, effort, permissionMode optional), or via .claude/agents files; programmatic ones win on name clash. Include Agent in allowedTools. Subagent messages carry parent_tool_use_id. Parent sees only the subagent's final message. Cap runaway fan-out with the two env vars plus maxBudgetUsd/max_budget_usd. Without a subagent_type, the built-in general-purpose agent is used.

Same page as above. Subagent spawned by the main agent runs in the background by default (Agent tool result status async_launched) unless Claude waits or background is set; a completed subagent's result text includes agentId, used with resume to continue it. Explore and Plan are one-shot and return no agentId. In-subagent permissions: plan/acceptEdits/auto/bypassPermissions inherit from the main session, but bypassPermissions is never applied to a subagent (v2.1.267+).
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Background-by-default subagents and fork subagents (v2.1.302) are recent behaviours.

docs_facts.fact: Capture session_id from the result message (also on the init system message in TypeScript), pass it as resume to continue that session with full context. continue (TS continue: true / Python continue_conversation=True) picks the most recent session in the directory. Fork a session with forkSession / fork_session to branch history under a new ID. Sessions persist the conversation, not the filesystem; stored under ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl and resumable on the same machine, or across hosts via a session store adapter. Python ClaudeSDKClient tracks the session automatically.

Enumerates sessions on disk: listSessions() in TypeScript, list_sessions() in Python. Companion helpers: getSessionInfo/renameSession/tagSession (TS) and get_session_info/rename_session/tag_session (Python). Use for session pickers and cleanup.
Reads a session's stored messages: getSessionMessages() in TypeScript, get_session_messages() in Python. Useful for transcript viewers.

The sessions page states sessions persist the conversation only and points to file checkpointing to snapshot and revert files the agent changed; forked agents' edits are real and shared. Option names and API of file checkpointing itself: not verified (its own page was not fetched).

Field on the SDK result message (success and error results alike): the cumulative estimated cost of the query() call, including subagent requests. It is a client-side estimate from a bundled price table, not billing data; use the Usage and Cost API or Console for billing. A resumed session's result already includes earlier spend, so read the latest result rather than summing. In Python the field is optional.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Resumed-session accounting changed at v2.1.277 (earlier, totals restarted at zero).

docs_facts.fact: Result-message map of model name to per-model token counts and cost (model_usage in Python); includes subagent requests, unlike the top-level usage field, which counts only the main loop. Entries carry costUSD, inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens, cacheCreationInputTokens, plus costBasis (list, managed, unknown; v2.1.246+). Per-step assistant-message output_tokens is a placeholder; read output totals from the result. Dedupe per-step usage by message id for parallel tool calls.

A built-in tool Claude uses to ask clarifying questions; in the SDK it always falls through to the canUseTool callback even if an allow rule matches, and is denied in dontAsk mode. It is removed entirely when --permission-prompts none is used. Handling details live on the user-input page (not fetched).
